newsitem.title: USA: Dole conceding most of Mid-Atlantic, Northeast-CNN.
newsitem.headline: Dole conceding most of Mid-Atlantic, Northeast-CNN.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole will focus in the final weeks of the campaign on winning votes in California and the West, but he is writing off most of the Mid-Atlantic states and the Northeast, CNN reported on Friday.
CNN, quoting Dole campaign aides, said the Republican challenger's strategy called for a major final push in all western and mountain states except Oregon and Washington.
Additionally, Dole would focus on winning the key states of Ohio and Michigan, as well as Indiana, Nebraska and his home state of Kansas.

Dole is heading to New Hampshire this weekend and would like to secure a victory there, but his aides told CNN he was writing off the states of Pennsylvania and New Jersey and the rest of the Mid-Atlantic, as well as the Northeast.
In an interview with the cable on-line network MSNBC, Dole said President Clinton's lead had narrowed to eight percentage points in California.
"We're going to spend a lot of time there, and we think we have an opportunity," Dole said.
He also predicted a win in Kansas, saying he might return to his hometown of Russell, Kansas to vote on Nov. 5.
Dole trimmed Clinton's lead to nine percentage points in the Reuters daily tracking poll released on Friday.
Clinton got 43.6 percent in the poll to Dole's 34.6 percent. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot scored 5.8 percent and 13.3 percent said they were still undecided.

The poll, conducted by John Zogby Group International, tracks about 900 likely voters over a three-day period. The latest result, with a 3.3 percentage point margin of error, reflects polling Tuesday through Thursday.
"I think the numbers are moving in our direction," Dole told MSNBC.
